title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 3rd Proof The Uniqueness Of Conveying The Message Summoning And Faith

questions.question: What main qualities did he show while delivering the message and calling people to the truth?
questions.answer: He showed strong determination, firmness, and courage.

questions.question: What kinds of opposition did he face according to the passage?
questions.answer: He faced resistance from powerful governments, other religions, and even from his own people, tribe, and uncle.

questions.question: How did he respond to that opposition?
questions.answer: He did not show fear, panic, or hesitation.

questions.question: What result of his mission is given as evidence of his unique strength in preaching?
questions.answer: He confronted the world successfully and Islam became dominant on a wide scale.

questions.question: How is his faith described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as exceptionally strong, deeply certain, wide in scope, and very elevated.

questions.question: What failed to weaken his faith?
questions.answer: The beliefs, ideas, philosophies, and teachings that were common in the world at that time could not shake it, even with strong hostility.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Companions and other righteous believers of later generations?
questions.answer: It says they drew from his faith and saw him as the highest example of belief.

questions.question: What conclusion did the traveler reach about truthfulness and dishonesty?
questions.answer: He concluded that someone with such unmatched law, religion, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith could not be a liar or deceitful person.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect idea is presented between his qualities and the traveler’s conclusion?
questions.answer: Because his mission produced unmatched results and his faith remained unshaken, the traveler saw this as proof of his honesty.

questions.question: What overall claim does this passage make about him in comparison with others?
questions.answer: It presents him as unequaled in delivering the message and in the strength of his faith.

questions.question: Which close relationships made the opposition especially difficult for him?
questions.answer: His own tribe and his uncle were among those who opposed him.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying he challenged the whole world?
questions.answer: It suggests that his mission was global in impact and that he stood firmly against very great opposition.

questions.question: According to the passage, what made his belief extraordinary besides strength?
questions.answer: It also had deep certainty, broad reach, and lofty conviction.

questions.question: How did the intellectual and religious climate of the time affect him?
questions.answer: It did not create any real doubt or weakness in him.

questions.question: What role do the Companions play in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: They serve as leading examples of believers who recognized the greatness of his faith.

questions.question: How do believers from later ages support the claim being made?
questions.answer: They are said to have taken from his source of faith and accepted him as the highest model of belief.

questions.question: What final judgment does the traveler make about lying and hypocrisy?
questions.answer: He decides that such faults cannot belong to a person with these unmatched spiritual and moral qualities.

questions.question: Which areas of excellence are listed together near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Sacred law, Islam, worship, supplication, calling to truth, and faith.

questions.question: What is the central message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: His unmatched courage and faith prove his truthfulness and sincerity.

questions.question: In the passage, what personal traits appear when he invites people to the truth?
questions.answer: He appears brave, steady, and unwavering.

questions.question: What is significant about the fact that even his own people opposed him?
questions.answer: It shows that the pressure against him was not only from outsiders but also from those closest to him.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying he showed no sign of inner disturbance?
questions.answer: It implies that his confidence in his mission was complete.

questions.question: How does the spread and success of Islam function in the argument?
questions.answer: It is presented as evidence that no one else matches him in conveying the message.

questions.question: What kinds of thought systems were unable to shake his belief?
questions.answer: Popular beliefs, philosophical ideas, and religious teachings of that time could not shake it.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by presenting his faith as a source or fountain?
questions.answer: It means others gained strength in belief by following his example and learning from him.

questions.question: Who are described as being at the front ranks of belief?
questions.answer: The Companions are described that way.

questions.question: What inference can be made from the way later saintly people viewed him?
questions.answer: They believed his level of faith was the highest and that he was the best model to follow.

questions.question: According to the traveler’s reasoning, why are falsehood and double-dealing impossible here?
questions.answer: Because the total greatness of his law, religion, worship, prayer, mission, and belief points to complete truthfulness.

questions.question: What two major themes organize this passage?
questions.answer: His firmness in preaching and his unmatched strength of faith.

questions.question: What challenge did he face when delivering the message?
questions.answer: He faced severe hostility from major powers, religious groups, and people close to him.

questions.question: Which character qualities helped him continue despite those challenges?
questions.answer: Courage, firmness, and perseverance helped him continue.

questions.question: What does the passage use as proof that his mission was not a failure?
questions.answer: It points to his success in confronting widespread opposition and establishing Islam strongly in the world.

questions.question: How is his certainty different from ordinary confidence?
questions.answer: It is described as extraordinary, vast, and so strong that it could not be shaken at all.

questions.question: What emotional states were absent from him in both preaching and faith?
questions.answer: Fear, hesitation, weakness, and anxiety were absent.

questions.question: Why are the saintly people of later generations mentioned?
questions.answer: They are mentioned to show that the best believers recognized his faith as the highest source and example.

questions.question: What does the passage say these saintly people did with respect to his belief?
questions.answer: They benefited from it and accepted him as the one with the greatest level of faith.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveler affirm in his mind?
questions.answer: He affirms that dishonesty and deception cannot belong to such a person.

questions.question: Name three areas in which the passage says he was without equal.
questions.answer: He was without equal in sacred law, worship, and faith.

questions.question: What broader lesson about truth can a student take from this passage?
questions.answer: Real truth shows itself through steady character, unshaken belief, and lasting beneficial results.

questions.question: What does the passage emphasize first: his knowledge, his wealth, or his steadfastness in calling people?
questions.answer: It emphasizes his steadfastness in calling people.

questions.question: How broad was the resistance against him?
questions.answer: It came from many directions, including political powers, religious communities, and his own relatives and tribe.

questions.question: What does his calm response to hostility reveal about him?
questions.answer: It reveals deep sincerity and strong trust in what he was sent to convey.

questions.question: What historical outcome is used to support his unmatched role as a messenger?
questions.answer: The spread and victory of Islam in the world is used as support.

questions.question: In what way was his faith untouched by surrounding ideas?
questions.answer: None of the dominant beliefs or intellectual systems could plant doubt in him.

questions.question: Why is it meaningful that hostility and denial did not weaken him?
questions.answer: It shows that his belief was not fragile or based on public approval.

questions.question: Who are said to have benefited from his belief across the ages?
questions.answer: The righteous people of later times, especially with the Companions at the front, benefited from it.

questions.question: What rank does the passage give him in the matter of faith?
questions.answer: It presents him as holding the highest degree of belief.

questions.question: What final moral judgment does the traveler make about his character?
questions.answer: He judges that lying and hypocrisy are completely incompatible with him.

questions.question: How does the end of the passage gather the earlier points together?
questions.answer: It combines his law, religion, worship, prayer, call to truth, and faith into one overall proof of his truthfulness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was remarkable about the way he called people to the truth?
questions.answer: He remained firm and brave even under intense and widespread opposition.

questions.question: What detail shows that the opposition was personal as well as public?
questions.answer: Even members of his own family and community stood against him.

questions.question: What does the passage present as a visible proof of his success?
questions.answer: It presents the strong establishment of Islam in the world as proof.

questions.question: Which words in the passage point to the depth of his belief?
questions.answer: The passage points to its strength, certainty, broadness, and high level.

questions.question: What sources of pressure could not disturb his inner conviction?
questions.answer: Existing worldviews, philosophical teachings, and religious traditions could not disturb it.

questions.question: How do the Companions strengthen the argument made in the passage?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as top believers who recognized and reflected the greatness of his faith.

questions.question: What does it mean that later holy people drew from his faith?
questions.answer: It means they treated his belief as a source of guidance and spiritual strength.

questions.question: What does the traveler decide after considering all these qualities?
questions.answer: He decides that deceit and false speech have no place in such a person.

questions.question: Which quality is connected to both his public mission and his private inner state?
questions.answer: Firmness is connected to both, since he was firm in preaching and firm in belief.

questions.question: Write the main idea of the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The passage argues that his unmatched courage in delivering the message and his unshakable faith prove his complete truthfulness.
